title: Zimbabwe Women Bank on West Indies Win for First India Tour
excerpt: Josephine Nkomo's unchanged squad opens its maiden bilateral series against India with a Raipur T20I on October 16, three weeks after a historic Harare victory.
body:
• Zimbabwe have kept the same 15-player squad, led by Josephine Nkomo, for their first-ever bilateral series against India, starting with the T20I in Raipur on October 16.
  • The squad earned its place with Zimbabwe's first-ever ICC Women's Championship win, a four-wicket victory over West Indies in Harare on September 27, built on Nyasha Gwanzura's career-best 4/33.
  • The tour runs three T20Is in Raipur (October 16, 18, 20) and three ODIs in Vadodara (October 23, 25, 28), with the ODIs counting toward the ICC Women's Championship.
  • The form line is mixed: Zimbabwe lost the West Indies ODI series 2-1 and the T20Is 3-0, so the India tour is a step up in class.

Zimbabwe's women will bank on the confidence of a landmark win over West Indies when they face India in a six-match tour that is a first for both sides. Zimbabwe have retained the 15-player squad that secured the country's first-ever ICC Women's Championship victory, for what the ICC described as their first-ever bilateral international meeting with India. The T20I series opens in Raipur on October 16.

The Win That Changed the Squad Conversation

The breakthrough came on September 27 at Harare Sports Club, where Zimbabwe beat West Indies by four wickets. Nyasha Gwanzura claimed career-best figures of 4/33 in that victory and keeps her place, alongside Michelle Mavunga and Francisca Chipare in the bowling group. Selectors have backed continuity over experimentation: the squad named for India is unchanged from the group that made that history.

The fuller record counsels realism. As Yardbarker's tour preview noted, Zimbabwe lost the West Indies ODI series 2-1 despite that one win, and the visitors swept the T20Is 3-0. The confidence is real, but it rests on a single famous afternoon rather than a run of results, and India at home are a stronger side than the one Zimbabwe beat in Harare.

Squad and Schedule

Captain Josephine Nkomo leads a group that mixes experienced names with younger batting talent. The full squad is: Josephine Nkomo (captain), Beloved Biza, Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano, Kelis Ndhlovu, Michelle Mavunga, Francisca Chipare, Olinder Chare, Kudzai Chigora, Nyasha Gwanzura, Nomvelo Sibanda, Loryn Phiri, Chiyedza Dhururu, Modester Mupachikwa, Tendai Makusha and Sharne Mayers. The batting group named by the ICC includes Mupachikwa, Mayers, Mugeri-Tiripano, Ndhlovu and Biza, with Nkomo and Sibanda adding international experience.

The three T20Is are in Raipur on October 16, 18 and 20. The tour then moves to Vadodara for ODIs on October 23, 25 and 28. The ODI leg matters beyond this tour because it counts toward the ICC Women's Championship, giving Zimbabwe a chance to add points against one of the championship's strongest teams.

What Success Looks Like

For Zimbabwe, a competitive series would itself be progress: taking matches deep, competing in the ODI leg where they recorded their historic win, and leaving India with championship experience their young players cannot get elsewhere. For India, the series is a home assignment they are expected to control, and a useful look at an unfamiliar opponent. For diaspora viewers, the Raipur opener on October 16 is the entry point, an evening T20I that sets the tone for whether Zimbabwe's Harare confidence travels. Whatever the results, a first bilateral tour between the two teams is a marker of how far Zimbabwe's women's programme has come since that September afternoon.
